## How the projects are structured

Each project begins with a clear **goal**, followed by **data and starting material**, a short **methods and evaluation** section and its level-specific scope. Bachelor work studies an established approach through a fair comparison. Master work develops or investigates an extension, such as improved robustness or transfer to new conditions.

A well-supported finding that a method does not help is a valid outcome.

Each project is labelled with one of three levels:

| Level | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **BSc or MSc** | Both routes are viable; choose the scope appropriate to your degree |
| **BSc only** | Offered at Bachelor level |
| **MSc preferred or MSc only** | Primarily offered at Master level; some list a reduced Bachelor version |

## What counts as a Bachelor or Master contribution

| Dimension | Bachelor project | Master project |
|---|---|---|
| Starting point | One dataset and one established method | Verified anchor-paper reproduction plus required baselines |
| Contribution | Documented pipeline, fair comparison and one focused ablation | New mechanism, protocol, graph/view construction or transfer/robustness study |
| Evidence | Correct split, sensible baselines and error analysis | Multiple seeds, uncertainty, matched budgets, ablations and resource reporting where relevant |
| Outcome | Explain whether and when the method helps | Answer the stated question; a controlled negative result is valid |

## Shared protocol for self-supervised projects {#shared-protocol-for-self-supervised-projects}

For projects that learn from unlabelled data, compare the pretrained model with an appropriate method trained without that pretraining. Where useful, test how performance changes when fewer labels are available. Agree the exact comparisons with the supervisor before starting.

Keep related measurements together: all data from one person, patient, household, engine, bearing or process cycle should stay in the same partition. For forecasting, train on earlier data and evaluate on later data. Choose evaluation measures that match the task.
